claims.assertion: The GPS track shows a genuine off-route segment between 12:27 and 12:36: 5.86 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.69 km, adding 3.17 km and reaching up to 1174 m away from the optimal route.

The driver's reroute was notified but the traffic facts do not support a 'reasonable cause' defence: no traffic incident was recorded near the route (F12), and the only speed reading is PIE band 4 (30–39 km/h), which is not band 1 or 2, so RD-4(a) and RD-4(b) are both unavailable.

The driver's chat request at 12:24 asked only for a route change via Sims Avenue and the rider agreed at 12:24; under RD-5 the segment is only exempt if the agreement precedes the deviation and its content covers that segment — the deviation ran 12:27–12:36, so the timing is satisfied, but the agreement covers 'Sims Avenue' only to the extent that the segment actually follows it, and any part of the 3.17 km extra that the rider did not agree to (including the 1174 m maximum excursion from the optimal route) remains a non-exempt detour.

This was a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the extra distance entered the fare: the fare facts bill 19.2 km at $1.41/km and show an excess-distance element of $5.31 for the 3.8 km over the optimal 15.5 km, and the total charged was $40.11.

The rider paid the whole metered total with no waiting or discretionary add-on to contest (waiting $0.00, platform $1.47 fixed, no surge), so the only disputed money is the distance attributable to the deviation, which should be refunded at the metered per-km rate for the non-exempt portion of the 3.17 km extra (F3) at $1.41/km (F4).

The driver ran this trip roughly a week after already having one upheld dispute in the last 90 days (driver 1 dispute, 1 upheld), so a repeat-conduct account flag is warranted alongside any refund; the rider's own record (0 upheld disputes) provides no ground for any action against the rider.

weaknesses: F7 and F8 (plus F9) show the driver asked about an alternative via Sims Avenue at 12:24 and the rider answered 'Sure, go ahead' at 12:24, i.e. before the 12:27–12:36 segment started (F3): the driver will argue RD-5 exempts the whole segment, and I can only carve out the part not covered by the agreed Sims Avenue route, which the route facts do not delineate.

The driver's 'reasonable cause' argument is weak on incidents (F12: none recorded) but F10 shows PIE at 30–39 km/h during 12:03–12:48, which the driver will use to argue F7's 'traffic building up' was honest even if band 4 does not meet RD-4; F13 (fair weather) also removes any weather excuse, so the driver will lean entirely on consent.

The single segment's extra_km (3.17 km, F3) does not equal the billed excess (3.8 km, F4), and the ~0.63 km difference is map-matching residue that cannot be attributed to this segment, so I cannot claim the full $5.31; my computable ask is capped by the 3.17 km figure and may be reduced further by any portion the court treats as consented under RD-5.

My client's own filed complaint relies on the estimate, but under the fixed-fare logic of F6 (metered RydeTAXI) only metered distance/units are recoverable — so the claim must stay within $1.41/km × non-exempt extra km and cannot include the $7.61 time charge or the platform fee (F6).

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the disputed money is the metered distance, not the quoted estimate: the fare facts show base $3.90, distance $27.13 for 19.2 km, time $7.61, platform $1.47, waiting $0.00, total $40.11, with the billed excess of 3.8 km valued at $5.31 [F4][F6][RD-2]. The GPS record shows a single off-route segment 12:27–12:36 driving 5.86 km where the optimal route covers 2.69 km, adding 3.17 km and reaching 1174 m from the optimal route, so a deviation exists and must be tested segment by segment under RD-1 [F1][F3][RD-1].

No traffic exemption is available: no incident was recorded near the route [F12], and the only speed readings are PIE and CTE at band 4 (30–39 km/h), which is outside RD-4(b)'s band 1–2 corroboration range and in any case cannot exempt on its own [F10][F11][F13][RD-4]. The driver's stated reason was therefore not a qualifying "reasonable cause" under the policy.

The segment is nonetheless exempt under RD-5. claims.assertion: The GPS track shows a genuine off-route segment between 12:27 and 12:36: 5.86 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.69 km, adding 3.17 km and reaching up to 1174 m away from the optimal route.

The driver's reroute was notified but the traffic facts do not support a 'reasonable cause' defence: no traffic incident was recorded near the route (F12), and the only speed reading is PIE band 4 (30–39 km/h), which is not band 1 or 2, so RD-4(a) and RD-4(b) are both unavailable.

The driver's chat request at 12:24 asked only for a route change via Sims Avenue and the rider agreed at 12:24; under RD-5 the segment is only exempt if the agreement precedes the deviation and its content covers that segment — the deviation ran 12:27–12:36, so the timing is satisfied, but the agreement covers 'Sims Avenue' only to the extent that the segment actually follows it, and any part of the 3.17 km extra that the rider did not agree to (including the 1174 m maximum excursion from the optimal route) remains a non-exempt detour.

This was a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the extra distance entered the fare: the fare facts bill 19.2 km at $1.41/km and show an excess-distance element of $5.31 for the 3.8 km over the optimal 15.5 km, and the total charged was $40.11.

The rider paid the whole metered total with no waiting or discretionary add-on to contest (waiting $0.00, platform $1.47 fixed, no surge), so the only disputed money is the distance attributable to the deviation, which should be refunded at the metered per-km rate for the non-exempt portion of the 3.17 km extra (F3) at $1.41/km (F4).

The driver ran this trip roughly a week after already having one upheld dispute in the last 90 days (driver 1 dispute, 1 upheld), so a repeat-conduct account flag is warranted alongside any refund; the rider's own record (0 upheld disputes) provides no ground for any action against the rider.

weaknesses: F7 and F8 (plus F9) show the driver asked about an alternative via Sims Avenue at 12:24 and the rider answered 'Sure, go ahead' at 12:24, i.e. before the 12:27–12:36 segment started (F3): the driver will argue RD-5 exempts the whole segment, and I can only carve out the part not covered by the agreed Sims Avenue route, which the route facts do not delineate.

The driver's 'reasonable cause' argument is weak on incidents (F12: none recorded) but F10 shows PIE at 30–39 km/h during 12:03–12:48, which the driver will use to argue F7's 'traffic building up' was honest even if band 4 does not meet RD-4; F13 (fair weather) also removes any weather excuse, so the driver will lean entirely on consent.

The single segment's extra_km (3.17 km, F3) does not equal the billed excess (3.8 km, F4), and the ~0.63 km difference is map-matching residue that cannot be attributed to this segment, so I cannot claim the full $5.31; my computable ask is capped by the 3.17 km figure and may be reduced further by any portion the court treats as consented under RD-5.

My client's own filed complaint relies on the estimate, but under the fixed-fare logic of F6 (metered RydeTAXI) only metered distance/units are recoverable — so the claim must stay within $1.41/km × non-exempt extra km and cannot include the $7.61 time charge or the platform fee (F6).

claims.assertion: This was a RydeTAXI metered trip (charged $40.11 by meter, base $3.90 + distance $27.13 + time $7.61 + platform $1.47, no waiting fee), so fare is distance-metered and the disputed amount is the billed excess distance of $5.31 for 3.8 km at $1.41/km.
There is exactly one off-route segment: 12:27–12:36, 5.86 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.69 km, adding 3.17 km and reaching 1174 m from the optimal route.

The rider expressly agreed to the route change before the driver left the optimal route: the driver asked at 12:24 whether he could go round via Sims Avenue and the rider replied 'Sure, go ahead' at 12:24 — earlier than the segment's 12:27 start — so this segment is a passenger-agreed routing request and not a deviation.

The rider named the place (Sims Avenue), so the substituted route satisfies RD-3(a) — the rider's named route is the new routing — and no stop or extra charge beyond the published fare items was added.

The driver's reason for rerouting is corroborated by the record: no traffic incidents near the route, and the expressway alternatives carried only band 4 (30–39 km/h) during 12:03–12:48 — this is the driver's reasonable-cause context and is not contradicted by any incident fact.
The driver has no upheld route deviations in 90 days (1 dispute, route: 0), so the RD-6 repeated-offence account flag does not apply to this case.

The complaint's core premise — 'I paid more than the estimate' — is a fixed-price complaint, but RydeTAXI is metered; the only amount traceable to the one off-route segment is the excess-distance portion of the meter, and that segment was rider-approved, so the correct outcome for that segment is no_action.

weaknesses: If the judge does not accept the 12:24 agreement as covering the actual 12:27–12:36 segment (F7/F8 against F3), RD-5 fails and the segment falls to RD-2: 3.17 km × $1.41/km ≈ $4.47 refundable — and RD-2 requires only that the segment be unexempted, not a percentage threshold (F1, F3, F4).

RD-4 does not exempt on traffic facts here: F10/F11 show only band 4 (30–39 km/h), above the band 1–2 'severe congestion' range, and F12 records no qualifying incident within 300 m of the optimal route — so the reroute cannot be justified by traffic alone; the driver must rely on the rider's agreement.
The route facts show a real, unexplained-by-traffic deviation of +3.8 km / +24% with one segment up to 1174 m off the optimal route (F1, F3), which is the fact the rider will lead with.

points.response: Agreed on the framework: RydeTAXI is metered, so the recoverable sum is metered distance and the billed excess-distance element is $5.31 for 3.8 km at $1.41/km (F4, F6) — we simply dispute that any of it was lawfully earned.

Accepted: one off-route segment 12:27–12:36, 5.86 km against 2.69 km optimal, +3.17 km, max 1174 m from the optimal route (F3); RD-1 needs no threshold, so this segment is presumed non-exempt unless an exemption applies.

RD-5 requires the agreement to cover the segment, not merely to precede it: the driver asked only for 'go round via Sims Avenue' (F7), while the recorded track of the segment reaches 1174 m from the optimal route and 5.86 km where the optimal covers 2.69 km (F3) — an excursion of that size is not shown to be the agreed Sims Avenue route, so the unmapped excess remains a non-exempt detour under RD-5.

RD-3(a) exempts a passenger-named place only where the detour does not arise from the driver's own choice of route; here the driver — not the rider — selected the path taken during 12:27–12:36 with 1174 m maximum divergence from the optimal route (F3), and the rider's message named a road, not a stop (F6 shows no stop, no waiting fee).

The driver's own 'traffic building up' reason fails RD-4: F12 records no incident near the route, and F10/F11 show only band 4 (30–39 km/h), which is not the band 1–2 range RD-4(b) requires — so the record contradicts the stated cause rather than corroborating it (F13 also excludes weather).

The 90-day record shows the driver with 1 dispute, 1 upheld (F15) — a prior upheld dispute — and RD-6's flag is sought as an additional action in light of that history, not as the basis for finding this deviation.

The premise mismatch does not defeat the claim: because RydeTAXI is metered, the only defensible exposure is the distance added by the one segment, 3.17 km at $1.41/km ≈ $4.47, measured from the GPS and fare records (F3, F4, F1) — the rider seeks exactly that and nothing more.

The existence of the segment is not in dispute — F3 describes one segment, 12:27–12:36, and that is the only deviation in the record; the question is only whether it is exempt, which RD-1/3/5 decide, not whether it happened.

Accepted that RD-4(a) and (b) do not exempt this segment: F12 records no incident near the route and F10/F11 show only band 4 (30–39 km/h), above the band 1–2 range — the driver's defence rests on RD-5 consent, not on traffic.

The rider named the place — 'Sims Avenue' in F7 — and answered 'Sure, go ahead' in F8 at 12:24, before the 12:27 start of the segment in F3; RD-3(a) makes a rider-named route non-deviating, and nothing in RD-3 or RD-5 lets the rider re-open a routing he named and expressly approved.

Not contested on the metering: F6 shows a metered 19.2 km total with distance $27.13 and F4 bills the 3.8 km excess at $1.41/km — but the metered excess is only recoverable under RD-2 when the segment is unexempted, and F7/F8 exempt it.

The rider's own admitted weakness is decisive: F3 attributes 3.17 km to the segment while F4 bills 3.8 km, so even on their own theory the ~0.63 km residue is map-matching noise that RD-2 expressly does not refund, and no fact in the table delineates any sub-part of the 3.17 km that was not agreed.

RD-6 requires an upheld route deviation (refund > 0 under RD-2 or a recorded RD-1 breach) plus route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; F15 shows route: 0 upheld and this case produces no RD-2 amount, and F14/F15 are profile facts that cannot themselves decide the case.

Withdrawn only in form: D3 stands on F7/F8/F3 for the timing and content of consent; I make no claim that the driver's traffic justification independently exempts the segment, so C2's point does not undercut the driver's case.
